title: Create direct Admin password participants

verify.attempt: Current implementation verification on real repository state
evidence: Focused Admin route tests passed creation of student and parent accounts, normalized login, duplicate-email denial, invalid parent-link rollback, and non-Admin denial.

Full Vitest suite passed 32 files / 147 tests; npm run check, npm run build, npm run e2e, and git diff --check passed against the real local application database without creating a product test account.

verify.attempt: Independent boundary review of current implementation
evidence: Review confirms Admin authorization is rechecked at the Center & Scheduling boundary, Identity & Access owns account/credential writes, the parent link requires an existing same-center student, and the surrounding transaction rolls back failed writes.

Review confirms the visible Admin path uses email/password, does not echo or persist plaintext passwords, leaves provider invitation compatibility intact, and removes lesson status/IDs from visible calendar cards.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-013 / REQ-001 / REQ-014 RED: the protected Admin surface cannot create a teacher, student, or parent with a direct normalized email/password credential and atomic center membership/parent link; GREEN: focused route tests and the real local browser smoke prove own-center creation, existing /login authentication, duplicate-email denial, invalid parent-link rollback, non-Admin denial, and the no-status/no-ID calendar presentation.
purpose: Allow an Admin to create teacher, student, and parent accounts directly with an email and a password, binding a parent to an existing student in the same center.
success_outcome: The visible Admin center form creates a server-owned participant account, password credential, center membership, and optional parent-student link atomically; the participant enters through the existing /login route.
anti_goals: Do not add OAuth, self-registration, password reset, email verification, MFA, or a second session/cookie lifecycle.
Do not trust client role, center, account, or student values for authorization; the server resolves the Admin scope and validates the selected student.
Do not create fake product accounts, seed synthetic fixtures, or reset the real local database during E2E.
Do not remove the legacy provider invitation implementation; it remains compatibility-only outside the visible direct-account Admin flow.

stop_conditions: Stop if direct creation requires a new auth store, dependency, provider, session type, or public route-owned persistence.
Stop if a parent can be linked to a student outside the selected Admin center or if a failed create leaves account, credential, membership, or link state behind.
Stop if real-DB E2E requires a synthetic product account or destructive database reset.

constraints: Center & Scheduling owns Admin scope, center membership, and parent-student link validation; Identity & Access owns account and password credential persistence.
Normalize email with trim().toLowerCase(), store only a salted Node scrypt result, and never return or echo the password from the server action.
Reuse the existing /login route, session cookie, and actor resolution; the visible Admin flow has no OAuth or invitation requirement.
Calendar lesson cards expose only the minimal day/lesson action text and retain no visible status or identifier labels.
invariants: Only an authenticated Admin in the target center can create a participant.
A parent link targets an existing student membership in the same center and is committed with the account, credential, and parent membership transaction.
Duplicate email or any invalid participant input leaves persistent state unchanged.
Password login uses the existing server-owned session lifecycle, and provider invitation code remains compatible.
verification_targets: FT-001-AC-013 / REQ-001 / REQ-014: RED: no direct Admin email/password participant path or atomic parent link exists; GREEN: protected action tests prove teacher/student/parent creation, normalized password login, duplicate-email denial, invalid-parent rollback, and non-Admin denial.

Account Provisioning Boundary: source and focused tests prove route transport does not write account/credential state directly, Admin scope is rechecked by Center & Scheduling, and Identity & Access receives the password provisioning command.

Real database smoke: browser login reaches the Admin center, renders the new account form, follows class/calendar/lesson navigation, saves and reloads existing lesson material, and restores the exact pre-existing data without product fixture creation.
Calendar presentation: rendered lesson cards contain the lesson action but do not show the status or lesson identifier text.
